letter.subject: Concern regarding cookie and tracking practices on hikma.com
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns identified during an automated, passive audit of https://hikma.com on 2026-11-08 04:10 UTC. Using a fresh browser, the audit visited the site, clicked the cookie banner option “I do not accept”, then browsed a small number of pages and recorded what was still set or sent.

The findings are as follows:

1. Our review suggests your cookie policy may be contradicted by the site’s behaviour. Google/YouTube tracking cookies were present before the banner was answered and remained present after rejection, while your policy states, “In most cases cookies cannot be deployed without consent.” This also appears inconsistent with the policy’s description of a system allowing users to give permission or deny cookies.

2. Google cookies were set before any choice was made. We observed 5 tracking cookies already set before the cookie banner was answered: VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE, VISITOR_PRIVACY_METADATA, YSC, __Secure-ROLLOUT_TOKEN and __Secure-YNID. VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE, YSC, __Secure-ROLLOUT_TOKEN and __Secure-YNID held what looks like a unique ID.

3. Google still received data after cookies were rejected. After clicking “I do not accept”, we observed 5 requests to google-analytics.com, googletagmanager.com and youtube.com.

4. One tracking company observed was not named in the privacy policy we reviewed at https://www.hikma.com/useful-links/privacy-policy/. The policy names 0 companies. We observed Google and found no mention of it, although the policy may describe recipients only by category.

5. google.com fingerprinted the device before any banner choice was made. Scripts from google.com (https://www.google.com/js/th/n_BHgtbTP3l_ff810bu_K6lL5wb_ZK3aoRJMIVk8Tks.js) used WebGL (GPU model) fingerprinting before the cookie banner was answered.

Please would you:

1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies and trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential cookies or tracking operating without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter is not resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker

controller_identity.label: Who is responsible (the controller)
controller_identity.quote: Where We process your personal data, the local Hikma company that has a relationship with you is considered the controller of your personal data.

purposes.label: What the data is used for
purposes.quote: We use information held about you in the following ways:

lawful_basis.label: The legal basis for using it
lawful_basis.quote: Most commonly, we will use your personal data for the performance of a contract or where it is necessary for our legitimate interests and your interests and fundamental rights do not override those interests.

recipients.label: Who it is shared with
recipients.quote: We may also disclose your personal information to third parties as follows:

retention.label: How long it is kept
retention.quote: We will only retain your personal data for as long as it is necessary to do so in order to achieve the purposes for which it was collected.

rights.label: Your rights (access, erasure, objection...)
rights.quote: You also have the right to ask Us to correct any mistakes in your information, to delete your personal data, or to provide you with a copy of your personal data to be used for your own purposes

withdraw_consent.label: How to withdraw consent
withdraw_consent.quote: You can also manage cookies via your browser settings (this will allow you to refuse the setting of all or some cookies)

complain_to_regulator.label: Right to complain to the ICO
complain_to_regulator.quote: You also have the right, if necessary, to lodge a complaint regarding the use of your personal data with a supervisory authority, which in the UK is the Information Commissioner’s Office.
